html:
The global security landscape is dominated by escalating tensions in the Middle East, where an attack on a UAE tanker in the Strait of Hormuz coincides with Iran’s declaration that the crucial waterway will remain closed until the United States changes its policies, even as a deal with Oman on shipping routes is reportedly close.

US Politics: Todd Blanche, a former personal lawyer for Donald Trump, has been narrowly confirmed as the US Attorney General, securing a major victory for President Trump despite strong opposition from Senate minority leader Schumer, who warned of 'pervasive, breathtaking corruption'. This confirmation, by a 50-49 Senate vote, positions Trump’s one-time criminal defense lawyer as the nation's top law enforcement official. Separately, Donald Trump is targeting birthright citizenship with two new orders.

Middle East Security: The attack on a UAE ADNOC tanker in the Strait of Hormuz, which the UAE attributes to Iran, has intensified the volatile situation, even as Iran and Oman report being "very close" to an agreement on a temporary shipping route. Despite this, Iran's security chief stated the Strait of Hormuz will remain closed until the US alters its policies towards Tehran, including ending military aggression and sanctions, a stance rejected by the Trump administration. Amidst this, the Chairman of the U.S. Joint Chiefs of Staff is reportedly seeking an exit strategy from the "war" with Iran, expressing concerns that military escalation might be counterproductive and that air power alone cannot achieve stated objectives.

Ukraine Conflict: Russia has continued its overnight missile and drone attacks near Kyiv, killing at least four people including a child, prompting warnings from President Volodymyr Zelensky about Ukraine’s dwindling supplies of missile interceptors. Simultaneously, Ukraine has escalated its long-range attacks on Russian energy facilities, striking another oil refinery in the Krasnodar region in an effort to fuel a growing fuel crisis in Russia. Meanwhile, President Zelensky is making his first official visit to Serbia, a country with close ties to Moscow, seeking to shore up international support and potentially acquire more arms.

Regional Alliances: A new mutual defense pact has been signed in Mecca by Saudi Arabia, Turkey, and Pakistan, an agreement described as a move towards a new regional security architecture amid the US-Iran "war" fallout. This pact would treat any act of aggression against one signatory as an attack on all. Concurrently, Yemen is teetering on civil war, with Houthi attacks killing at least 58 Saudi-backed Yemeni government forces and wounding 11 in Saudi Arabia, drawing condemnation from Jordan and other regional entities.

European Tensions & Latin American Shift: Intra-European tensions have escalated as Spain imposed border controls against Italy, citing an intensifying row over an influx of approximately 78,000 migrants from Morocco into the Spanish exclave of Ceuta. In Latin America, Abelardo de la Espriella has been sworn in as Colombia's new right-wing president, receiving $1 billion in US support and promising an "all-out war" on "narco-terrorism."

Global Economy & Natural Disasters: Gold prices are set to record their largest weekly gains since January, while oil prices are rising amid concerns about navigation in the Strait of Hormuz. In other news, Typhoon Dolphin has battered Japan's Okinawa, cutting power to thousands and injuring five, before bearing down on China. Separately, former US president Joe Biden's prostate cancer has spread throughout his body, causing him significant pain, according to his son Hunter Biden.
